URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/dollar-holds-yen-gains-as-equity-rout-saps-risk-appetite-ahead-of-payrolls.html
Outlet: CNBC (Reuters copy), published Fri Nov 6 2026 12:03 AM EST, updated Fri Nov 6 2026 11:39 AM EST
Dollar index jumps after U.S. payrolls beat forecasts

Dollar Index: surged 0.63% to 102.12 (on pace for its biggest daily percentage gain in seven weeks)
Euro: tumbled 0.55% to $1.1157
Sterling: dropped 0.62% to $1.3366, pulling back following a climb to a more than seven-week high on Thursday after the Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in over three years
Japanese Yen: weakened 0.3% to 158.20
Nonfarm Payrolls: 165,000 jobs (vs. 65,000 Reuters-poll estimate); unemployment rate 4.1%
10-Year Treasury Yield: up 3.1 bps to 4.868%
2-Year Treasury Yield: up 5.5 bps to 4.532%
Fed December hike expectation: ~80%

Eugene Epstein, Moneycorp: "It's the same old conversation of, at any given moment, is the dollar trading more on a safe-haven basis, or is it trading more on an interest rate differential basis?"
John Williams, New York Fed President: inflation "is too high and it is essential to bring it back to 2%."
Philip Lane, ECB Chief Economist: goal is ensuring inflation can be returned to 2% "over the next year or two."
